notes.title: Update 4 OUT NOW and VR Launch Update!
notes.content:
[p]Greetings, Commanders![/p][p][/p][p]The fourth post-launch update which comes with a huge list of improvements, balancing and fixes is out now. These include a special focus on post-game content: "[b]Threat Levels[/b]" and a re-work of the [b]Overclock[/b] system.[/p][p][/p][p]We have an update regarding the VR version coming to Steam. Due to an unexpected technical issue with the game, the launch of the VR version has been delayed to next week. We apologise for this inconvenience and want to ensure that you have the best possible experience when playing. We promise to keep you updated on the situation and to let you know once the VR version is officially out next week.[/p][p][/p][p]Thank you so much for understanding and for always supporting our game, in the mean time, we hope you enjoy the changes in update 4. We'd love to hear what you think, so let us know by joining our [url="https://discord.gg/xd3dnxUDR5"]Discord server[/url] and sharing your feedback.[/p][p][/p][h2]Threat Level Rising[/h2][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45039714/889b4d26d98cfacd32a00ef871647a05b4606a96.jpg"][/img][/p][p][b]Threat Levels[/b] have been activated across all regions, marking the beginning of [b]a new post-game campaign[/b]. Each region now comes with [b]five escalating Threat Levels[/b]. The further you push, the tougher enemies become.[/p][p]
Every Threat Level comes with a set of [b]Directives[/b], high-risk challenges that must be completed in a single mission. Succeeding earns you [b]Medals, Command’s new currency[/b] for unlocking higher Threat Levels.[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45039714/987381d2077754e3885f131d30e02a68aaa6af07.jpg"][/img][/p][p]Combat balance has been overhauled to match the rising challenge, so expect tougher fights, tighter margins, and deadlier choices. The [b]War Room’s[/b] been retooled to support this new structure. You’ll find Threat Levels front and centre in mission prep, making it easier to track your progress and plan your next deployment.  [/p][p][/p][p]To read more about Threat Levels, check out [url="https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/1911860/view/499455821076234421"]our preview post from last week[/url].[/p][p][/p][h2]Overclocks Reforged[/h2][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45039714/d216011ea36869f4876aee63893a74b9e9c897f7.jpg"][/img][/p][p]We also recently posted a preview of the Overclocks re-work! [url="https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/1911860/view/499455821076234423"]You can find it here in case you missed it[/url].[/p][p][/p][p][b]Overclocks[/b] are no longer tucked away in the Mech Yard, but now [b]earned in the thick of battle[/b]. You’ll unlock and equip them mid-run, shaping your firepower and tactics in [b]real time[/b]. If you spent Intelligence or Blueprints unlocking Advancements or Overclocks before, Command’s issuing full refunds.[/p][p]
Overclocks are now organised into [b]10 specialist categories[/b], each one pushing your mechs in a new tactical direction. Not every mech can access every category, so you’ll need to know your unit and [b]make your choices count[/b].[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45039714/77d295cf6e2695ed4da41bb133d7d5015f3b5687.jpg"][/img][/p][p]Power (the way Overclocks are unlocked) has also changed. It’s now [b]fuelled directly by Boosts and Enhancements[/b]: each one you slot in adds to your [b]Overclock ‘Power’ capacity[/b]. We’ve lowered the thresholds to get you into the action faster, and you’ll see your Power Level front and centre when selecting upgrades. [/p][p][/p][p]We also added a [b]new Overclock reward screen[/b] and upgraded the Squad Overview so you can track your build at a glance.[/p][p]
Command is also dropping [b]43 brand-new Overclocks[/b] into the rotation. Some existing ones have been reworked, others reassigned as Enhancements, and one decommissioned entirely. [/p][p][/p][h1]Changelist[/h1][h2]Threat Levels[/h2][list][*][p]Added Threat Levels which scale the difficulty of the region.[/p][/*][*][p]Added Directives which reward Medals to unlock Threat notes.title: Post-Launch Update 2: Chain of Command
notes.content:
Greetings, Commanders!

With this update, our goal is to put tactical command firmly in your hands. We're introducing new tools to coordinate your squad with greater precision, whether it’s by locking onto high-value targets, setting unit-specific priorities, or issuing instant regroup orders in the heat of battle. 

Every change is designed to deepen your strategic options and reward smart decision-making on the field.

[h2]Tactical Improvements[/h2]

[h3]New Command: Regroup[/h3]

When things get messy, you need to pull back fast and smart. That’s where Regroup comes in. One command, and every unit in your squad will rally to a point you choose. No fumbling, no delay. You can issue it with a quick click of the Regroup button at the bottom right of your HUD, or by using your assigned keyboard or gamepad binding. Use it wisely, it might just save your squad.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45039714/edaafae6c0157e2ee85ca371c01149c4760cc8d4.gif[/img]
[h3]New System: Target Priorities[/h3]

Outnumbered? Surrounded? Doesn’t matter, what matters is who you hit first. With the new Target Priorities system, each of your mechs follow orders the way you see fit. You set the rules, they execute. Choose from the following priorities:
[list]
[*] Type
[*] Weak
[*] Healthy
[*] Injured
[*] Far
[*] Close
[/list] Access this feature through the Squad Overview by clicking the button on your HUD, or use your assigned keyboard or gamepad binding. Once you’re in, you’ll see toggles on each unit to set their priorities.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45039714/7ee3095b1750b04fadb114c3d5217e4bb7bf994f.gif[/img]
[h3]New Option: Focus Fire[/h3]

Sometimes it’s not about who's the biggest threat, it’s about finishing the job. With Focus Fire, your units will stay locked on their target until it’s scrap, no matter what else steps into range. You can toggle this setting for each unit in the Squad Overview.

[h3]New Command: Mark Target[/h3]
With this new command, you can manually designate a priority target on the battlefield using your mouse or gamepad cursor. Once marked, that enemy will be focused down by your squad, ignoring all other orders.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45039714/b40d4ce53c7c4051c901fcb4edb993cb71306aad.gif[/img]
[b][h2]Thank You, Commander [/h2][/b]
Before we get into the rest of the update changes below, we wanted to say a thank you for your continued support. To celebrate the latest update, we’re giving all players a new Command Vehicle skin which you'll be automatically granted upon downloading the update. This is our way of showing appreciation for being part of the Resistance. Equip your new looks, hit the battlefield, and show your enemies what style under pressure really looks like!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45039714/e89f68af46928aed8d3ce653c366e54b2b0da254.png[/img]
[h2]General Improvements[/h2][list]
[*] Mechs and Pilots already assigned to your squad can now be selected in Squad Select to more easily compare stats.
[*] Squad Select layout has been refined for improved clarity and ease of use.
[*] You can now compare current vs. new modules more clearly when viewing modules in the Mech Yard.
[*] Fusing Modules in the Mech Yard now provides additional information about potential resulting modules.
[*] Ability attribute values are now shown in the Pilot Barracks.
[*] The Squad Overview open/close animation has been sped up for a smoother experience.
[*] Attributes in Squad Overview are now navigable, with tooltips displayed when an attribute is selected.
[*] Overclocks are now visible within the Squad Overview.
[*] Boosts in Squad Overview now display the exact stat increase they provide.
[*] Removed General Larkin’s voiceover warnings for Critical Hits and High Ground damage.
[*] Added a new voiceover from General Larkin when the Command Vehicle takes damage.
[*] Increased the size of damage numbers during gameplay for better visibility.
[*] Boss phases are now indicated on the boss’s health bar during fights.
[/list]
[h2]Bug Fixes[/h2]
[list]
[*] Fixed bosses not highlighting correctly in High Contrast Mode.
[*] Fixed boss level objectives not highlighting correctly in High Contrast Mode.
[*] Fixed destroy objectives not highlighting correctly in High Contrast Mode.
[*] Fixed 'Pilot Mute' option not working.

[*] Fixed fusing tutorial not progressing correctly when using keyboard or gamepad bindings.

[*] Fixed 'Squad Overview' key bind being called 'Enhancements' in settings menu.
[*] Fixed the extract tile indicators still showing after the extract vehicle has been destroyed.
[*] Fixed the extract vehicle still occupying its tile after being extracted.
[*] Fixed Command Vehicle not displaying the correct skin on the HUD.
[*] Fixed an issue where tooltips did not update after upgrading an ability in the Pilot Barracks.
[*] Fixed tooltips on Run History covering up most of the information.
[*] Fixed tooltips on Squad Overview making gamepad navigation difficult.
[*] Fixed boost tooltips not having names.
[*] Fixed boost tooltips width being incorrect.
[*] Fixed access denied tooltip not appearing on Command Centre when it is locked.
[*] Fixed enhancements for dead mechs appearing as a choice when awarded.
[*] Fixed Jump Jet not displaying correct stat values for kills and damage dealt.
[*] Fixed reroll text on rewards screen not displaying correctly when it is affordable.
[/list]As always, we appreciate your feedback and support. Share your thoughts and experiences with the update in our [url=https://discord.gg/8eqDpa88nf]Official Discord server[/url].

[i]The Grit and Valor - 1949 Team[/i]

notes.title: Dev Diary #2: Cover Deep Dive
notes.content:
Hey everyone – Kevin here again with another Dev Diary! This time, we’re diving deeper into one of the core gameplay mechanics: Cover.

Since launch, we’ve gotten a lot of feedback about how cover works in the game – especially around our decision to make it 1-sided (offers protection in only one direction) instead of 2-sided (protection from both directions).

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45039714/bc59c5ddbdf7238dd7f7e1f8581decc71f6b3b98.png[/img]

To be honest, most of the feedback has leaned critical, or at least confused. Outside of our dev team, not many players have spoken in favor of 1-sided cover – and even within the team, there are folks who’d prefer the 2-sided approach.

These kinds of design choices are always tricky during development, so I wanted to share a bit of insight into how we made the call, and what the pros and cons of each setup look like.

[b]1-sided Cover[/b]
Pros:
[list]
[*] Encourages more strategic positioning – players need to be mindful of where enemies are coming from.
[*] Promotes level exploration, as players move around to find cover that works based on the direction of threat.
[*] Gives players a tactical advantage – enemies are much less likely to benefit from cover.
[*] Cons:
[*] Doesn’t always make sense visually – why would a wall only protect from one side?
[*] Can be frustrating when a seemingly good piece of cover becomes useless just because enemies show up from the "wrong" direction.
[/list]
[b]2-sided Cover[/b]
Pros:
[list]
[*] Feels more intuitive and realistic – a wall should offer protection on both sides.
[*] Makes cover more universally useful, which could help reinforce it as a core mechanic instead of something players forget about.
[*] It adds to the tactical challenge – if enemies use cover against you, that’s on your positioning. You either take the cover yourself or deny it to the enemy by repositioning.
[/list]
Cons:
[list]
[*] Players might end up dancing around a single block of cover depending on enemy spawns, rather than moving around the map. (see diagram below).
[*] If cover takes damage from both sides, it could get destroyed really quickly. That might balance things out and make players move around the map more, but could also make cover feel weak or temporary.
[/list]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45039714/44721ffad3fdabcc72c03dd00423b6e418a0bbcb.png[/img]
We have started to prototype 2-sided cover and discovered a couple of bugs so far but generally the bulk of the work would come from going into each level and making sure:
[olist]
[*] Cover isn’t  too advantageous if it suddenly became 2-sided, and possibly therefore stripping some cover out or moving it around.
[*] Cover isn’t too weak now it takes damage from both sides and needs a further balance pass on each level (or again some rearrangement).
[/olist]
As you can probably tell, we’re still torn on which direction to go. We’d love to hear your thoughts to help us decide!

In the meantime, we’ll keep testing and share more updates in the next Dev Diary.

Thanks for reading everyone – and enjoy your weekend!
Kevin

notes.title: Dev Diary #1: Post-Launch Reflections
notes.content:
Hi everyone, Kevin here — Producer on the project.

It’s now been around six weeks since the game launched, and we’ve had some time to reflect on the release, the state of the game, and all the feedback we've received. I wanted to take a moment to share some of those reflections with you and give a clearer picture of where we’re heading.

[h3]Launch and First Impressions[/h3]
Game launches are never easy. You spend years building something, then release it into the world and hope that players connect with it as deeply as you do. It’s an emotional moment — a mix of relief, joy, and (let’s be honest) a bit of fear, and a lot of hitting "refresh" on Steam reviews!
That said, we’re really proud of the game we released. The launch went smoothly overall, and while reviews have ranged from okay to good, we’re taking everything on board. A 77% review score in the strategy genre isn’t bad — especially given how savvy and discerning this audience is. The general consensus seems to be: “There’s a solid foundation here, but room for improvement.” We agree.

[h3]Top Themes in Player Feedback[/h3]
Here's a quick summary of the key feedback we've seen so far:

[list]
[*] Core gameplay is fun but lacks tactical depth
[*] Core gameplay is fun but lacks variety (e.g., things you experience in runs and ability to change things up mid-run)
[*] The roguelite grind can feel frustrating
[*] Game balance needs further refinement
[*] Certain gameplay elements feel frustrating (notably: Hazards, repetitive VO, and the Cover system)
[*] Some players expected a turn-based experience similar to Into the Breach
[/list]

There’s a lot to unpack here. We're a small team, so we’re taking things step by step — prioritising, testing, and listening. While I can’t promise every piece of feedback will be addressed immediately, I can promise to keep sharing what we’re working on and to keep the conversation going.

[h3]What We're Working on Right Now[/h3]
Here’s what we’re currently focused on (and I’ll dive into these more in future posts — some of them deserve their own breakdown):

[h3]Cover - 1-sided vs. 2-sided[/h3]
There’s been plenty of feedback to say that cover should be two-sided, one-sided cover doesn’t make sense etc. and we understand where people are coming from. Cover has always been one-sided to make it a clear tactical advantage to the player rather than something that enemies will also benefit from....but given the weight of feedback, two-sided cover is something we’re testing out.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45039714/e98027c64010b48f74600dc23b7282d4cee4556d.gif[/img]

[h3]Re-group Command & Enemy Prioritisation[/h3]
Players have been asking for more tactical control and less micro-management — a tricky balance, but one we’re working toward. To help with that, we’ve been testing a new regroup command, along with a feature that lets you set priority levels for your units. Both of these should cut down on the need for constant individual clicks and repositioning, while still giving you room to plan more strategically — without slowing things down for players who prefer a more fast-paced, action-heavy style.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45039714/95ad85828193e497b3f56d2496905d714d037232.gif[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45039714/5764ba85225e64d643b60edb8e1152a7832caa61.gif[/img]

[h3]Surfacing more useful information[/h3]
Players have been asking for clearer, more detailed info to help make better choices around upgrades and progression. We’re updating menus and tooltips to show more stats — including comparisons where it makes sense. So far, we’ve focused on areas like the Pilot Barracks and Ability stats, Mechyard tooltips, and the run overview. We’ll keep refining and expanding as we go.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45039714/602dff698a5d29165312506991ae65fc71ed6931.png[/img]

That’s it for now — just a quick update to let you know where our heads are at. Massive thanks to everyone who’s played the game, shared feedback, or just taken the time to care. It really does mean a lot.

Thanks everyone,
Kevin

notes.content:
Greetings, Commanders!

[h2]Wargames Fest - Demo Back Online![/h2]
Before we dive into the update notes - we're delighted to be a part of the ongoing Wargames Fest on Steam. To celebrate, we have put our free demo back  online. so it's the perfect time to try Grit and Valor for free and share it with your friends.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45039714/803eb5a5c43ddcbb3b5e66a83fa2744d166b7f1d.png[/img]

[h2]Update Notes[/h2]
The first of three post-launch updates has arrived! As promised, we focused this month's changes on improving the experience for new players and getting them into the action quickly. The update also brings a series of quality of life improvements and bugfixes.

Here's what's changed:

[h3]Early Game Improvements[/h3]
[list]
[*] [b]You now begin with a full squad from the start of the game with Thunderhead unlocked.[/b]
[*] Valor Currency can now start being earned after the first run instead of only after the Pilot Barracks is unlocked.
[*] After finishing the tutorial you now go back to the Resistance Base.
[*] The tutorial no longer awards black coins on completion.
[*] Reduced power needed to activate Overclock slots from 10, 15, 20 to 4, 12, 20.
[/list]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45039714/d34e3f3c8f5845eb6eb6e03f2872f7b9e73438fb.png[/img]
[h3]Command Center Improvements[/h3]
[list]
[*] [b]Command Center Advancement tab is now displayed as a tech tree, showing future unlocks.[/b]
[*] Command Center upgrades have been re-arranged and costs adjusted.
[/list]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45039714/3d5ba78bb88b6e7982074b81857c3621601bbe35.png[/img]
[h3]Control Improvements[/h3]
[list]
[*] Adjusted the size and position of units' selection colliders to make them easier to select.
[*] The camera now adjusts its pivot to match the height of the tile in the center of the screen, making it easier to select high ground tiles near the edges of the map when using a gamepad.
[*] When using a gamepad, the camera moves to the middle of the nearest tile when you stop panning.
[*] The path and range indicators no longer appear when hovering over a tile you cannot move to.
[*] The path and range indicators now update correctly when selecting units with the 1-4 hotkeys on keyboard or cycling through them with the bumpers on a gamepad.
[*] An outline now appears on the tile you are currently hovering over if a unit can move to it.
[/list]
[h3]UI Improvements[/h3]
[list]
[*] On the Region Map, you can now navigate to future level nodes to view their tooltips when using a gamepad.
[*] While navigating the Region Map with a gamepad, the map now auto-scrolls to frame the currently selected level node if it is offscreen.
[*] Moved the Main Menu panel and Pause Menu panel closer to the middle of the screen when using an ultrawide resolution.
[*] Added a smooth scrolling effect to some menus.
[*] Slightly increased the height of the Settings Menu to show an additional item in the scrollable list.
[/list]
[h3]Game Balance[/h3]
[list]
[*] Increased Health and Armor of all enemies in Western Europe by 10% and increased damage by 8%.
[*] Increased Health and Armor of all enemies in New Germany by 15% and increased damage by 13%.
[/list]
[h3]Bug Fixes[/h3]
[list]
[*] Fixed units walking on top of each other when passing by on ramps.
[*] Fixed Savage Momentum Enhancement at Rare rarity increasing damage by 75% instead of 7.5%.
[*] Fixed Weakness Damage Boosts not appearing as a Boost Reward Choice.
[*] Fixed the Scandinavia boss mech not appearing during its intro cutscene.
[*] Fixed the currently selected level not being framed correctly when returning to the Region Map and using a screen resolution other than 1080p.
[*] Fixed Disruptor and Revenge Field Repairs Augments not triggering correctly.
[*] Fixed focus loss that could occur when failing a level or retreating which prevented reward cards from being claimed when using a gamepad.
[/list]
Thanks as always for your continued support! We'd love to hear your thoughts on the above changes, especially once you have tried them in-game. Let us know what you think here on Steam or in the official [url=https://discord.gg/8eqDpa88nf]Grit and Valor[/url] and [url=https://discord.gg/xd3dnxUDR5]Megabit Discord[/url] channels.

notes.title: Patch Notes: Display Settings and Other Fixes
notes.content:
Greeting, Commanders!

Following your bug reports and feedback we have implemented the following changes:

[h3]Display Settings Fixes[/h3]
We have overhauled the system for managing display settings to address cases that were not fixed by the previous patch. The changes include:
[list]
[*] When you change the resolution, display or window mode and select Apply in the Settings menu, the game now saves your changes without re-applying them.
[*] When you make changes in the Settings menu and select Revert, the game applies your previously saved display settings and refreshes the settings text once the changes have finished applying.
[*] When you select Defaults from the Settings menu, the game returns to your main display (the first one in the Display list) and uses that display's native resolution in Borderless window mode. If the native resolution is reported as portrait, the game translates it to landscape.
[/list]
[h3]Known Issues and Limitations[/h3]
[list]
[*] The UI is designed for a minimum aspect ratio of 16:10 (commonly used on laptops and handhelds), so we don't recommend using any narrower resolutions. The 4:3 and 5:4 resolutions are automatically filtered out.
[*] Portrait displays such as vertical monitors are not supported, so the game may behave unexpectedly if you try to move the game window to them.
[*] When setting the Window Mode to Fullscreen and using a resolution other than the display's native resolution, the game may not display correctly. If you need to use a non-native resolution, we recommend using Borderless window mode.
[*] You may see unusual resolutions in the list which are larger than your display's native resolution (e.g. some 1440p monitors may also list 4K as an option). This is normal as the game reads from the same list of resolutions available in Windows Display Settings, even if they cannot be applied.
[/list]
[b]Please Note[/b]
If the game launches in an incorrect resolution or does not let you select a playable resolution after installing this patch, please follow these troubleshooting guidelines:

[b]Reset Settings to Defaults[/b]
The game may be trying to load an invalid resolution that was saved in a previous patch, so please try reverting your settings to defaults. If you cannot do this in-game, follow these steps:
[olist]
[*] Close the game.
[*] Delete your Settings.ini file which can be found in this folder: %USERNAME%/AppData/LocalLow/MilkyTea/Grit and Valor
[*] Launch the game again.
[/olist]
[b]Report a Bug[/b]
If you have tried the above and the game still does not display correctly, please follow these steps to send us more information so we can debug the issue:
[olist]
[*] In your Steam Library, right-click the game and select Properties, then go to the Betas tab and enter the password fixthescreens. 
[*] Opt into the mt_debug_display branch which should appear.
[*] Download and install the beta update.
[*] Launch the game.
[*] Open the Display Debugger menu from the top of the screen. This menu is centered horizontally so it should be accessible even if the game launches in a narrow resolution.
[*] Take a screenshot of the game while the Display Debugger menu is open (press F12 to capture via Steam).
[*] Upload your screenshot and send it to us either in this Steam discussion or in the bug-reports channel on the Grit and Valor Discord.
[/olist]
[h3]Other Fixes[/h3]
[list]
[*] Fixed Bomber Plane not appearing in the Advanced Combat levels in New Germany.
[*] Fixed dead units causing navigation issues and units to spin on the spot.
[*] Fixed tile issues in Western Europe levels in which inaccessible tiles were selectable, causing mech pathing issues.
[/list]
Thanks for your patience while we have dealt with these bug reports. We appreciate all the feedback and will continue investigating any future reports. You can share your experiences here on Steam or via the official [url=https://discord.gg/8eqDpa88nf]Discord[/url].

[i]The Grit and Valor - 1949 Team[/i]

notes.title: Mech Analysis: Warbringer
notes.content:
Greetings, Commanders! 

Introducing the Warbringer, an Explosive Class mech designed for maximum impact. Manufactured by Warhead, this heavy-duty powerhouse comes equipped with dual launchers, allowing it to strike multiple enemies simultaneously. Whether bombarding enemy squads or softening up fortified positions, the Warbringer ensures no target is safe from its devastating firepower. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45039714/0c2e7000bbe81fc8579477bc3b0259321ea2a5ed.jpg[/img]
[h3]KEY STATISTICS [/h3]
The Warbringer is a force to be reckoned with in any battle, thanks to its high Fire Rate and ability to deal sustained damage across multiple targets. While its Damage per shot is modest, its rapid Fire Rate ensures it can consistently lay down heavy fire over a wide area, overwhelming your enemies and supporting the squad. 

The Warbringer can take considerable damage before going down, though it relies on your positioning and support to endure. Movement Speed is moderate, making it less nimble than faster mechs but still capable of staying in combat without being too slow. 

Its Weapon Range allows it to engage most threats at medium distances while remaining out of range from many close-combat enemies. Its rapid fire rate ensures plenty of opportunities for consistent damage output. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45039714/3caa84b98593b2a6f51d3102cf340bd8b034f344.png[/img]
[h3]ABILITY PAIRINGS [/h3]
With the right ability pairings, the warbringer can turn it into a relentless force on the battlefield. 

[b]Archie Miller - Mech Jet:[/b] The Warbringer's moderate speed means it can struggle to reposition quickly. The Mech Jet ability allows it to traverse the battlefield with ease, getting into better firing positions or escaping overwhelming encounters. This can be especially useful when taking advantage of the High Ground Damage bonus, letting it reach elevated terrain for maximum impact. 

[b]Jan Novak - Deploy Mines:[/b] Since the Warbringer's rapid firepower can lock down areas, Deploy Mines provides an excellent defensive tool to complement its offensive capabilities. Place mines ensuresenemies take additional damage while trying to evade its barrage. 

[b]Emilia Rochefort - Mechano-arm:[/b] The Mechano-arm provides much-needed health regeneration, allowing it to remain in combat longer and sustain its relentless firepower without requiring frequent retreats. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45039714/5a1a3f7e5d8993d8ec49d71cc2dc160f07c2e09a.png[/img]

With the right strategy, the Warbringer becomes an unstoppable force, raining down destruction on multiple enemies at once. Its high fire rate and area control make it a formidable asset in any squad, especially when paired with abilities that enhance its positioning, survivability, and battlefield dominance. Stay tuned for more intel on the remaining mech models! 

Stay up to date on game news and more by joining us on Discord!

notes.title: Update: Control Scheme Improvements
notes.content:
Greetings, Commanders!

Thank you as ever for your determined efforts to liberate the British Isles! Your feedback and reviews throughout the demo have been incredibly helpful. Based on your suggestions, we’re making changes to the controls. These are now live in the demo and will also feature in the final release on 26 March.

[b]NOTE: Existing players will need to reset controls to default for some of these changes to take effect.[/b]

[h2]General Improvements[/h2]
[h3]Unit Cycling[/h3]
Previously, Cycling Units would default to the same mech, making moving your whole squad tedious with this method. It looked something like:
[olist]
[*] Press Cycle Units which would select the first unit (e.g. Ironclad).
[*] Move Ironclad to a tile, at which point the Ironclad gets deselected.
[*] Press Cycle Units, which selects the Ironclad again.
[*] Press Cycle Units again for it to then Select the next unit (e.g. Draqan).
[/olist]
Now, the system will automatically move along to the next unit in order by default to help you cycle through them more quickly.

[h2]Keyboard + Mouse Changes[/h2]
[h3]Left Click/Right Click[/h3]
Units are now selected with the left mouse button and moves with the right mouse button by default. This is more in line with other RTT and RTS games. The units’ colliders have also increased in size, making them easier to select quickly. We hope this makes manoeuvring your squad more fluid!
Gamepad and touch controls remain in the one-button style for convenience on those control schemes.

[h2]Gamepad Changes[/h2]
[h3]Unit Cycling[/h3]
Cycling through units is now bound to the left/right bumpers by default (previously left/right on the d-pad). This allows you to cycle through units at the same time as controlling the camera more easily.

[h3]Freeze Time[/h3]

notes.title: Resistance Pilot Profile: Emilia Rochefort
notes.content:
It’s time you got to know the pilots under your command in Grit and Valor - 1949. 

In the coming weeks, we’ll be sharing some detailed intel on our brave Resistance pilots and how you can make the most of their abilities on the battlefield. Starting with Emilia Rochefort!

[h2]Emilia Rochefort: Repair Pilot[/h2]
[b]Nationality: [/b]French
[b]Age:[/b] 22
[b]Special Ability:[/b] Mech Repair

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45039714/0c438b193f812b797c3fe1ff8f8ef059577f674f.png[/img]

[b]Biography[/b]
Growing up on a farm in a rural Alsace village, Emilia was fascinated with the way things worked. From an early age she’d take apart her toys and household appliances just to put them back together again. She was always tinkering with something. As she grew older, she began repairing and greatly enhancing her family farm’s agricultural equipment. 

By 18 she'd already become an immensely talented engineer, but when the Axis invaded Emilia's family farm was reduced to ash. She joined the Resistance soon after, applying her exceptional skills to the Resistance’s new Mech Command division.  
  
[b]Personality Traits[/b]
Emilia is deeply curious, always seeking to understand the "why" behind everything. Her unmatched resilience drives her to believe that nothing—whether a machine or a mech—is beyond repair. This hopeful outlook drives her on the battlefield where she is pragmatic, focused, and unwavering. 
  
[h2]Pilot Special Ability: Mech Repair[/h2] 
Naturally, Emilia Rochefort’s mechanical prowess allows her to make on-the-fly repairs to the mechs she pilots on the battlefield.  
 
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45039714/25e6a368a4dcdf9bcf8307c8267aa9e74a376a81.gif[/img]
 
This Ability can be effective in several ways. Use it offensively – deploying Emilia’s mech on the front line and effectively turning your mech into a ‘tank’ unit, soaking up damage before repairing yourself. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45039714/e219c57ec41b05cca188ffd4cb10fa3a7361abcb.gif[/img]

Alternatively, you can use it defensively, keeping your repair ability in reserve for a noble last stand.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45039714/10eff1192c1892d211624eca9e38caba5a1094fd.gif[/img]

Whichever way you choose to deploy it, Emilia's Special Ability can have a significant impact on your chances of surviving a run - so be sure to use it!

notes.title: Upcoming Features Deep Dive #1 – Run Rewards!
notes.content:
[b]Attention, Commanders! [/b]
 
We've received fresh intel on upcoming changes to Grit and Valor’s Run Rewards systems. 
 
As mentioned previously, your feedback on the demo has been helping our teams massively in finding new ways to make Grit’s tactical gameplay sing.  

Now that the Closed Beta is live, we’re going to be delving in to a wealth of additional feedback. Here’s an overview of some changes to rewards that are already in the works! 

[h2]WHAT ARE RUN REWARDS?[/h2]

If you’re a Roguelite/Roguelike veteran – feel free to skip ahead! 
 
If you’re new to Roguelites, a ‘Run’ is what you begin each time you’re defeated on the battlefield. 
 
Run Rewards, then, represent the progression you make over the course of a run. 
 
To make matters more complex – in Roguelites this progression can be split in two; Standard Progression and Meta Progression. 

 [img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45039714/13f90d87f47e56edce23befc3c61488ba353f22f.png[/img]
 
In the case of Grit and Valor – 1949, ‘Standard Progression’ represents the temporary enhancements you get during a run. 
 
‘Meta Progression’ represents the permanent upgrades you’re able to make back at the Resistance Base and carry with you in future runs. 
 
[h2]RUN REWARD IMPROVEMENTS: STANDARD PROGRESSION[/h2]

[h3]Reward Frequency[/h3]

We noticed that only offering mid-run upgrades at the end of a mission meant long breaks between upgrading your squad over the course of a run!  
 
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45039714/0f61ba1d9562b87a692a5f00e42185380e7cf7d1.gif[/img]
 
In future you’ll notice rewards "dropping" during a mission. You’ll need to assess on the fly whether to bring your Mechs out of cover to go procure them, adding an entirely new risk-vs-reward dynamic to your moment-to-moment gameplay. 

[h3]Improved Enhancements[/h3] 

To make choosing enhancements and going for a specific build more meaningful, we’re going to improve their effects and even create synergies between different Enhancement types. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45039714/d3b7279019d802ef217af8937def03005ba7a972.gif[/img]

[h2]RUN REWARD IMPROVEMENTS: META PROGRESSION[/h2]
 

[h3]New Pilots![/h3]

We’ll also be introducing some new Pilots – each with unique never-before-seen abilities! We can’t wait to tell you more about them in a later blog...

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45039714/9957fad903ee627454811c1466d9c19c867c9f8c.png[/img]
 

[h3]Pilot Ability Augmentations[/h3] 

We’re also exploring new ways to give you more control over how you set up your squad. In the future, Grit and Valor will allow you to augment existing Pilot Abilities to make them behave exactly the way you like. 
 
Take the Mech Jet Ability, for instance. With Pilot Ability Augmentations, a cautious player could augment this ability mid-run to be able to jump then immediately jump back to its starting position. Alternatively, an offensively minded Commander could augment that same ability to drop mines as it jumps. 
 
We took your feedback and some inspiration from other satisfying Roguelite systems for this! It should give you even more variety on each run! 
 
--- 

We hope this has given you some valuable insight into how we’re using your feedback to improve the game’s rewards system ahead of launch. In the coming weeks, we’ll be sharing more of these deep dives on other aspects of Grit and Valor Gameplay! 

If you’d like to help with future changes, [url=https://www.surveymonkey.com/r/LLHGHCV]apply to our Ambassador program[/url] where we hold regular playtests. You can also [url=https://discord.gg/8eqDpa88nf]join our Discord[/url] for extra behind-the-scenes content! 
 
[i]The Grit and Valor – 1949 Team[/i]

notes.content:
[b]Attention, Commanders! [/b] 
Today, we're thrilled to reveal the British Isles Boss and deliver important intel on Boss Levels - an exciting never-before-seen aspect of Grit and Valor: 1949! Boss Levels are the final stage of each region and pit your squad against a devastating Axis Boss Mech. 

[previewyoutube=5G1qwG7b9tE;full][/previewyoutube]

We're also announcing an upcoming Closed Beta - don't miss your chance to join!

In this blog, we’ll provide you with backstory on the British Isles Boss, an overview of Boss Level mechanics, and a closer look at the Boss Mech design. Before we begin, however, we have even more exciting news!

[h2]Join Our Closed Beta in December![/h2]
To test the game’s improvements off the back of the demo, we’re running a closed beta from 2nd – 9th of December. 

[url=https://bit.ly/4fCCUdc][b]***CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR DECEMBER CLOSED BETA!***[/b][/url]

This new version of the game will feature: 
[b][list]
[*]Three NEW Mechs! 
[*]Harmsworth's Boss Level! 
[*]Revamped Rewards System!
[*]Revamped Upgrades System!
[/list][/b]
This is the perfect opportunity to see how your feedback has driven the game so far and help refine it even further with more suggestions! 

[h2]British Isles Boss: General Harmsworth[/h2]
A fat cat of the highest order, General Harmsworth was once Britain’s richest Media Baron. Using the power of his newspaper empire, Harmsworth kept his pockets lined and heavily influenced political opinion.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45039714/ce5247e9a8eb0971a32b4f070d6a2623daf3fb2c.png[/img] 

 [i][b]"People used to think that the way to rule was with an iron fist inside a velvet glove.  I have taken off the velvet glove. And it feels wonderful."[/b][/i] [b]- General Harmsworth[/b]

When Axis forces invaded, Harmsworth took the opportunity to betray his country - coordinating a coup against the British government which hastened the collapse of the Allied forces. 
 
Now a high-ranking Axis Commander, he subjugates the British civilian population while attempting to hunt down and crush the Resistance. 

[h2]General Harmsworth’s Mech[/h2]
Harmsworth’s personal Mech is perhaps the only thing even more monstrous than the man himself.  

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45039714/adfc4b95963206bbb2616656f659e5575229bb1c.gif[/img]

A terrifying quadruped that dwarfs all other known mechs, this machine is big enough to cast its shadow over entire towns.  All who have stood in its way have perished.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45039714/541a9f16050cb205169e10c001c7af97c386a50a.png[/img]

Built in the image of its owner, Harmsworth’s mech is an imposing and seemingly unstoppable force equipped with an arsenal of weapons systems to make it effective against any opponent.

[h2]Boss Level: Gameplay & Mechanics[/h2] 
With unprecedented hazards, waves of elite reinforcements, and Harmsworth’s Boss Mech, The British Isles Boss Level will be your squad’s greatest challenge yet. 
 
To overcome this monstrosity, you’re going to need to adapt the way you play...

[h3]Keep Moving[/h3]
High-calibre machine guns. Flamethrowers. Mortar firing capabilities. Harmsworth’s Boss Mech has a means of overpowering any Mech type. Whittle down the boss’ health while keeping your squad in rotation to ensure their weaknesses aren’t exposed!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45039714/3c2bd22935df535c103972f4834dc52ca9bf15d1.png[/img]

[h3]Avoid Hazards and Defeat Elite Reinforcements[/h3]
As the highest-ranking Axis General in the British Isles, Harmsworth has access to entire battalions of air and land reinforcements. Avoid bombing runs and don’t underestimate Elite Infantry and Mechs.

notes.title: Upcoming Features!
notes.content:
Since releasing the demo for Grit & Valor, we’ve learned a ton about what makes roguelite and tactical games feel rewarding—and we can’t wait to bring that experience to life. We’ve gone through every comment, crunched the game data, and we can’t wait to show you what’s coming next. Here’s an overview of what’s in the works!

[h2]Run Rewards [/h2]
Get ready for major improvements to the rewards you’ll score both mid-run and back at base! We’re dialling up the impact of your choices, adding more variety, and making every decision feel bigger and bolder.
 
[olist]
[*] [b]Reward Frequency + Mid-Run Rewards:[/b] we noticed that only offering mid-run upgrades at the end of a mission meant long breaks between upgrading your squad over the course of a run. We’re looking at "dropping" upgrades during a mission, causing players to choose whether they can risk collection. 
[*] [b]Playstyle-Altering Rewards:[/b] taking inspiration from upgrades like the Daedalus Hammer in Hades, you will be able to augment Pilot Abilities, fundamentally changing the way they behave. We expect this to greatly increase the uniqueness of every run. 
[*] [b]Improved Enhancements:[/b] to make choosing enhancements and going for a specific build more meaningful, we’re going to improve their effects and create synergies between different Enhancement types.
[/olist]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45039714/ae55b69fb0533d31d7b446eca3eebb9b8134654c.jpg[/img]
[h2]More Pilots and Abilities[/h2]
Our demo contained four Pilots, each with a unique ability. To increase varirety, we’re examining options such as allowing duplicate pilot abilities within a squad as well as adding more abilities. Each option would offer both more content to unlock throughout the game and greater variety! 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45039714/9957fad903ee627454811c1466d9c19c867c9f8c.png[/img]
[h2]The Opening Gameplay Experience[/h2] 
In the demo, players went from controlling one Mech in a safe environment during the tutorial to controlling three plus the Command Vehicle in a live mission. To help familiarise first-time players with the mechanics, unlocking Mechs and Pilots will be made more gradual. 
 
Similarly, Pilot Abilities appeared to add a layer of complexity too early on and were underused in early levels. Gradual unlocking and UI improvements to better communicate when abilities can be used will make this easier.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45039714/a6dafabff3d858b1a53e05094cb9e0b3012e81e0.png[/img]
[h2]Combining the Mechyard and Scrapyard [/h2]
Moving between the Mechyard and Scrapyard to buy modules and then upgrade mechs was more cumbersome than we would like. Combining these spaces should streamline the upgrading experience by requiring fewer steps.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45039714/cfc6fd2e41ed86db67e69d4c2d603c8323b8304e.png[/img]
[h2]Casual Mode [/h2]
To offer a fun experience to our more casual audience, we’re working on a more forgiving difficulty. This will likely be stat-based and allows us to maintain the current level of challenge for players who prefer it.

[h2]The Command Centre [/h2]
The Command Vehicle will receive its own progression system, via the Command Centre, a new location within the hub. Here, you will be able to unlock and upgrade further abilities for the Command Vehicle, making it more integral and useful part of the squad in battle. 

The Command Centre will also allow players to unlock other mechanics and progression systems within the game.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45039714/c18e8f37471b5a5a21e0ceca2a9fa0c43fb34841.png[/img]
[h2]Region Map Changes [/h2]
[olist]
[*] [b]Random Narrative Nodes:[/b] having the option to choose a narrative node missed an opportunity for spontaneous moments. We’re addressing this by introducing more choice, strategy and variability into the Region Map. Our exploration here is designed to make these events feel more natural when they arise.
[*] [b]Reviving Mechs:[/b] losing a mech during a run can be devastating, especially if your build focused on enhancing that specific type. Shop nodes and starting currency will be adjusted to make it easier to buy back a mech, especially if one is lost early in the run.
[/olist]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45039714/cd58e296ed0a184867fcfd28951e365bd5849986.png[/img]
[h2]Highlighting Time Controls[/h2]
Many players in the demo found and enjoyed the time controls allowing the game to be slowed down or even paused while they assessed and issued commands. However, due to time constraints, these were only previously available via the Settings menu and unbound by default. These controls will be added to the UI along with other general UI improvements.  
 
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45039714/102ec32c48ddf647ccaf876979ae97ea3d0fa1c0.png[/img]
Thank you again for your support! We’re thrilled to keep improving Grit & Valor - 1949 with your feedback and look forward to sharing more updates soon! Over the coming weeks, we’ll dive into these changes in more detail.

If you’d like to help with future changes, [url=https://www.surveymonkey.com/r/LLHGHCV]apply to our Ambassador program[/url] where we hold regular playtests. You can also [url=https://discord.gg/8eqDpa88nf]join our Discord[/url] for extra behind-the-scenes content! 
 
~ The Grit and Valor – 1949 Team

notes.title: Grit and Valor – 1949 | Progression & Upgrades Explained
notes.content:
[b]Attention Commanders![/b]

In Grit and Valor – 1949, each run pits your mech squad against overwhelming odds. 

To liberate Europe from the evil Axis Forces, you’re going to need to make the most of every upgrade and enhancement you can get your hands on.   

So buckle in!  

Here's a 101 on the ins and outs of the progression system, and how your decisions can be the difference between disastrous defeats and valiant victories.   
 
[h2]How Progression and Rewards Work[/h2]  

For fans of the Roguelite genre aspects of this may be familiar, but let's get into the specifics. 
 
In Grit and Valor – 1949, there are three core aspects to the progression system: 

[olist]
[*][b]Mid-Run Progression[/b]:  

During each campaign you’ll have the opportunity to boost your mechs with a choice of temporary end of level enhancements. You’ll also get the chance to buy temporary shop boosts and get narrative event rewards.
[*][b]End-of-Run Rewards[/b]:  

When your run ends, you’ll bank a range of meta currencies to spend back at the Resistance Base. Occasionally, you’ll unlock new pilots, too.
[*][b]Between-Run Progression[/b]: 

At the Resistance Base, you’ll spend your earned currency on mech modules that you can equip to permanently upgrade your mechs. It’s here that you’ll able to purchase new mechs, and level up your pilot abilities.
[/olist]

Now, let's explore these in more detail...  

[h2]Mid-Run Progression[/h2] 

In Grit and Valor – 1949, mid-run progression is all about building up temporary enhancements to increase your chances of success, while banking Black Coins to spend along the way. 

[h3]Enhancements[/h3]

Enhancements are temporary stat upgrades for your mechs that last until your run ends. At the end of each successful mission, you’ll be presented with a choice of three.  

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45039714/1ad22d950948e4e1b8b53878280fe5d23ca22ac9.png[/img]

Enhancements range from Common to Legendary and can offer big boosts to a variety of mech stats including damage, damage resistance, fire rate, critical damage and much more.  
 
Remember to choose wisely. Picking enhancements that suit your mech squad and your playstyle is essential. If you’re dissatisfied with your roll, spend some Black Coins to reroll. 

It’s important to note that opting to take on Advanced Combat and Elite Combat missions will give you a greater chance of picking up rare enhancement. These missions are far more deadly, however, so we’ll leave it to you to weigh up the risk vs reward. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45039714/a7406cc8cafc56ca3b3a73722e9950f574354786.jpg[/img]

[h3]Scenarios[/h3] 

Between levels, you’ll occasionally be given the choice to avoid combat altogether and instead progress by choosing a ‘Scenario’ - a narrative dilemma that requires your Commander instincts. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45039714/4ddeee095878d372f18f9f74b4ca240563e04c47.jpg[/img]

Scenarios will vary in content – and we wouldn’t want to spoil any narrative bits - but in this example, you find a broken Axis mech and can choose between salvaging it for a random enhancement and using its part to repair your mechs or give them a health boost for the remainder of your run. 

[h3]The Scavenger’s Shop[/h3]

Another mid-run opportunity for you to enhance your squad is the Scavenger.  

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45039714/780e9a0ee35a14eb00cb8615c5ca4c621e673898.jpg[/img]

Like Scenarios, you’ll encounter the Scavenger on the campaign map between missions and be given the option trade your Black Coins for enhancements or Scrap. These run-ins with the Scavenger are rare, but could save your squad in a pinch. 

[h2]End-of-Run Rewards[/h2] 

End-of-Run Rewards come in the form of Scrap, Valor, and Blueprints.  

These are the essential resources you’ll need to use to acquire lasting upgrades back at the Resistance Base, such as new Mechs, enhanced Pilot abilities, and Upgrade Modules for your existing Mechs. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45039714/8f4be99f6bce0518fee9493eeb48916072ee8977.jpg[/img]

The amount of Scrap, Valor, and Blueprints you gain will depend on your run's success. 

Tackling those Advanced and Elite missions, achieving your bonus goals, and eliminating more Axis forces will increase the amount you receive at the end of a run. 

Here’s a little more on what each currency is used for: 

[list]
[*] [b]Scrap[/b] - A currency used to purchase Upgrade Modules from the Junkyard Shop at the Resistance Base.
[*][b]Valor[/b] - Valor is applied to individual Pilots at the Pilot Barracks to increase their skills.  
[*][b]Blueprints[/b] - Blueprints can be used to either unlock new mechs or buy traits for them at the Mech Yard.
[/list] 

[h2]Between Run Progression[/h2] 

Here’s where you can make a lasting impact. Upgrades you make to your Mech Squad back at Resistance Base are permanent. Let’s dive into what you can do.  

[h3]Buy Mech Modules at the Junkyard Shop[/h3]

Spend your scrap wisely at the Junkyard Shop on Upgrade Modules for your Mechs. Like Enhancements, Modules range from Common to Legendary.  

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45039714/3538a720dde5b113c9e7aa0ec9d613ff94b58e2d.jpg[/img]

[h3]Apply Modules and Traits at the Mech Yard[/h3] 

Once you’ve purchased some Upgrade Modules, head to the Mech Yard to have Reggie Steele apply them to your mechs. 

Optimise your squad however you see fit. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45039714/69544f81488f1ed6ff2384f14a8aa869217ee4ef.jpg[/img]

In this example, the Commander has wisely addressed one of the Thunderhead’s weaknesses, movement speed, by equipping a +30% Module. 

[h3]Unlock New Mechs[/h3] 

At the Mech Yard – if you have acquired enough blueprints, you can use them to requisition the development of powerful new mechs. 

[h3]Upgrade Pilot Abilities[/h3] 

Next stop, the Pilot Barracks. 

Providing your Pilots with the Valor they need to succeed is part of every capable Commander’s pre-run ritual. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45039714/305d9d395c4b089fb8e60df7ec2560d9f147e5b3.jpg[/img]

Here, Emilia Rochefort’s Mechano-arm ability has been boosted. In combat, you’ll now be able to use the ability more often and it’ll repair more damage. 

---
 
Congratulations, Commander. You’ve passed your Progression & Upgrades 101 with flying colours.  

Now what’re you waiting for? Go and apply what you’ve learned in the field. 

Let ‘em have it!

notes.title: Grit and Valor – 1949 | Play the Demo!
notes.content:
Greetings Commander!  
 
We’re delighted to announce that Grit and Valor – 1949: is now available to play in our Steam demo! In preparation, we’re sharing this brief on your ultimate objective of freeing Europe mission by mission, region by region. 

Your goal as Commander of the Resistance is to deliver the EMP weapon and disable the Axis Machine Tower in the heart of New Germany. To get there, you will traverse four regions, freeing them from the enemy’s occupying forces along the way. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45039714/4cfeee635e9f9be2e06c02db0313e453d85b02be.jpg[/img]
To progress through a region, you must dive into a series of missions and defeat waves of enemies. This is achieved by moving your squad of three mechs and the all-important Command Vehicle and responding to the evolving battlefield in real-time. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45039714/237a813ac943c83354f89475740a0314e3f74ccf.png[/img]
Choosing the right position for your mechs is critical. Here are some tactics to bear in mind:  

[list]
[*] Place your mechs between enemies and your Command Vehicle to protect it 
[*] Use elevated tiles to gain a Critical Damage bonus against enemy units 
[*] Engage enemy units with mechs that have a damage type-advantage 
[*] Shield your mechs using cover 
[/list]
When you have mastered these tactics, you may also complete Bonus Objectives if you are daring enough! These include capturing radio towers and defending important buildings. Doing so rewards you with Black Coins which can be spent on upgrades in the Scavenger’s shop during your run.  

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45039714/75348069bd2cdf3ac9df013d81b3a2e7aa1491ef.jpg[/img]
As you complete missions, you will carve your path through the region. Along the way, you can choose which missions to take to maximise your chances of success. Here are some factors which might influence the direction you take:  

[b]Enhancements:[/b] choose temporary upgrades to work best with your squad build. Some missions offer a greater chance of rare Enhancement rewards. 

[b]Black Coins:[/b] Bonus Objectives reward the Black Coin currency (in-run upgrades). 

[b]Scavenger Supplies:[/b] An encounter with the Scavenger offers the chance to spend your Black Coins on replenishing squad Health, Mech Armor, Enhancements and more. 

[b]Hazards and Elites:[/b] Missions featuring Hazards such as enemy Bomber Planes or Elite enemy mechs offer an increased chance of rare Enhancement rewards. 

Region Events: Chance encounters along the journey offers the player a difficult choice, and possible rewards and dangers. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45039714/f68c009f5c5758afb9ce4b0ba231288393d820fb.jpg[/img]
When your run is over, you will also be rewarded with Scrap, Valor, and Blueprints. These currencies allow you to purchase permanent upgrades in the Resistance Base such as new Mechs, improved Pilots skills, and Upgrade Modules for your existing Mechs. 

The amount of Scrap, Valor, and Blueprints you’re rewarded with will scale depending on your performance in the run, by completing more missions, bonus objectives and taking down more of the Axis forces your rewards will increase. 

We trust this overview will help when the time comes to free regions from the grip of the Axis Powers. Should you fail, you can return to base to make necessary upgrades and redeploy. We will share more intel on how to build the ultimate mech squad in a future transmission. 

To stay up to date on news and announcements join our Discord server and sign up to our newsletter! 

[i]The Grit and Valor – 1949 Team [/i]
